message.content:
I don’t have real‑time market data, so I can’t give you the exact price of gold for today.  As of the most recent publicly available quotes (late‑2023/early‑2024), gold was trading roughly **$1,950–$2,000 per troy ounce** in U.S. dollars.  The price can swing by a few dollars in a single day, so it’s best to check a live source for the current figure.

**Where to get the up‑to‑date price**

| Source | Typical update frequency | Notes |
|--------|--------------------------|-------|
| **Kitco** (goldprice.com) | Every few seconds | Provides live spot prices and charts. |
| **Bloomberg** (markets section) | Every minute | Includes news and analyst commentary. |
| **Reuters** (markets) | Every minute | Offers a global view of precious metals. |
| **Investing.com** | Every few seconds | Shows price in multiple currencies. |
| **U.S. Treasury or Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)** | Daily | For official settlement prices. |

If you need the exact price for a specific time, you can look up the “spot” price on one of those sites or use a financial data API (e.g., Bloomberg Terminal, Alpha Vantage, or Quandl).

We can provide a general answer: gold price is around X per ounce, but we need to be careful. We can say approximate price or say that we don't have real-time data. We can suggest checking reliable sources. We can also provide a typical price range. We should not fabricate. So answer: I don't have real-time data, but as of last known data, gold was around $... per ounce. Provide approximate. Also mention that price fluctuates. Provide suggestion to check Bloomberg, Kitco, etc.
